day: Saturday of week 23 in Ordinary Time or The Most Holy Name of Mary or Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary
text:
When Jesus speaks about trees bearing fruit according to their nature, he is not scolding us for a moment of failure. He is asking us to notice something true: what we fill ourselves with shapes what flows out. The cup we drink from matters. The table we gather at leaves its mark on us.

Paul's warning about communion echoes this gently. He is not condemning anyone but inviting us to ask honestly: what am I taking in? Where am I truly placing my trust? These questions are tender, not harsh. They assume we know the difference between what nourishes and what hollows us out. A good tree, Jesus says, draws goodness from deep within, from a store laid down over time through small choices, through what we have let settle into our hearts.

The foundation matters most when the flood comes. We cannot build our lives on borrowed words or empty promises to God. Real life is built on listening and doing, on the slow work of letting Christ's words take root in us, day after day, until they become part of our deepest self. This is how we become sound trees, bearing good fruit not because we strain for it, but because something true and living grows within.

You might sit quietly with one image today: the tree, the cup, the foundation. Which one speaks to your heart right now?
